angle: Why the first three NIST post-quantum standards serve two distinct purposes

items.claim: FIPS 203, 204, and 205 were approved in August 2024.
items.synthesisExcerpt: The Secretary of Commerce approved FIPS 203, 204 and 205 in August 2024.
items.sourceEvidence: NIST page, operator paraphrase: “The Secretary of Commerce approved FIPS 203, 204 and 205 in August 2024.”
items.qualification: Does not describe their later adoption.

items.claim: FIPS 203 specifies ML-KEM for establishing a shared secret over a public channel.
items.synthesisExcerpt: FIPS 203 specifies ML-KEM to establish a shared secret between parties communicating over a public channel.
items.sourceEvidence: NIST page, operator paraphrase: “FIPS 203 specifies ML-KEM to establish a shared secret between parties communicating over a public channel.”
items.usefulness: Establishes one purpose of the standards.
items.qualification: The excerpt does not describe the protocol or its use.

items.claim: FIPS 204 specifies a module-lattice-based digital signature scheme.

items.sourceEvidence: NIST page, operator paraphrase: “FIPS 204 specifies a module-lattice-based digital signature scheme.”

items.qualification: The excerpt gives no further detail about the scheme.

items.claim: FIPS 205 specifies a stateless hash-based digital signature scheme.

items.sourceEvidence: NIST page, operator paraphrase: “FIPS 205 specifies a stateless hash-based digital signature scheme.”
